rule: SettleInvoice is never called for an invoice of an order fulfilled by another invoice; after reconciliation every superseded or late invoice is canceled in LND, so no order has two payable invoices.
message: p0 called SettleInvoice for o1#1, a late invoice (recorded not-created, LND holds it ACCEPTED) although order o1 has live invoice o1#2 (open); it is to be canceled in LND, never settled
note: The 1.4 audit's RECV-A. Hold invoice o1#1's AddHoldInvoice is cut in transit; the creator's lookup finds nothing within the creation window, so it stays creating (steps 0-2). A reconcile looks it up (3); the window passes (4); the create reaches LND late, o1#1 OPEN (5), and the customer pays it: ACCEPTED (6). `receiver settle` selects o1#1 (the order's live hold invoice) and looks it up (7). The reconcile's stale NotFound lands: o1#1 is decided not-created (8). o1#2 is issued and OPEN (9-10). The settle's lookup answers ACCEPTED for o1#1 (11): the record was decided not-created meanwhile and o1#2 is the order's live invoice, so o1#1 is a late invoice, to be canceled in LND by the settle itself (12-13 answer its CancelInvoice and the lookup after it), never settled. The mutant calls SettleInvoice for it: o1#1 fulfills the order and o1#2 stays payable.
